description:
Milestone per ARCHITECTURE.md §12 v0.3.

Success criterion (quoted): Agent can invoke at least two tools (bash, read_file). Tool calls are commits. Large tool outputs auto-dispatch to a parsing invocation. Tool contract (binary + schema + skill) documented.

=== Scope ===
- Two worker-callable tools: bash, read_file. Each implemented per §3.3 as binary + JSON schema + SKILL.md.
- Tool calls land as commits on the exchange branch, with records under steps/NNN/tool_calls/<tool-id>/ per §2.2.
- Provider wire-up: the model emits tool_use blocks; the harness feeds matching tool_result blocks on the next step per §2.5 ("every tool returns synchronously").
- Tools are reachable via the CLI dispatcher (§3.4). In-process tools implemented as built-in subcommands invoked the same way as external ones.
- Tool contract documented: §3.3 pinned against shipped shape; TAXONOMY/PRINCIPLES updated if any new terms of art are introduced.

=== Explicit non-goals ===
- Auto-dispatch on oversized tool output (§3.3 last bullet; §3.4 mention). Deferred: the sizing heuristic and parsing-invocation handoff lean on v0.4's subagent dispatch machinery and aren't worth baking into the base spec yet. Flagged in docs as deferred; revisited alongside v0.4.
- Handle-based async / await(handle) (§2.5). v0.3 tools return synchronously and inline.
- Worker-level subagent dispatch (v0.4).
- UI (v0.5), workflow.yaml (v0.6), task suite (v0.7), experiments/replay (v0.8).

=== Done-when ===
End-to-end: a prompt that drives the model to emit tool_use blocks for bash and read_file resolves into tool_call commits on the exchange branch, exchange rebases and --no-ff merges back to main. Tool contract documented and coherent with §3.3. All three gates closed.
title: v0.3: tools
